subject: CSEC Mathematics
question: O is the centre of a circle. A and B are points on the circumference and ∠AOB = 104°. A tangent is drawn at A. Calculate the angle between the tangent and chord AB.
worked_solution: OA = OB, so ∠OAB = (180° − 104°)/2 = 38°. The radius is perpendicular to the tangent. Required angle = 90° − 38° = 52°.

misconception.label: Gave the angle at the centre
misconception.remediation_hint: Angle AOB = 64 degrees is the apex of the triangle, not a base angle.

misconception.label: Forgot to halve when finding the base angles
misconception.remediation_hint: 180 - 64 = 116 must be shared between the TWO equal base angles.

worked_solution: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference: angle AOB = 2 × 32 = 64 degrees. OA and OB are radii, so triangle OAB is isosceles and angle OAB = angle OBA. angle OAB = (180 - 64) / 2 = 116 / 2 = 58 degrees.
hints: Angle OAB is a base angle of triangle OAB, which must be worked out.
Angle AOB = 64 degrees is the apex of the triangle, not a base angle.
180 - 64 = 116 must be shared between the TWO equal base angles.
common_mistakes: Copied the angle at the circumference
Gave the angle at the centre
Forgot to halve when finding the base angles
learning_objective: Apply circle theorems involving the centre of a circle.
exam_skill: Combine the angle-at-the-centre theorem with the isosceles triangle formed by two radii
prerequisite_skills: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
Base angles of an isosceles triangle
